Neuroscientist Andrew Gallimore joins Danny Jones to talk about people who take DMT and map the worlds they visit. The episode title calls them psychonauts charting hyper-dimensional space. Gallimore studies the drug and the brain in his lab work.

Gallimore explains why the DMT world feels so fixed and shared from trip to trip. He walks through the maps that users draw of that place and its beings. Jones asks whether the map proves a real place or just a shared brain state. Listeners get a clear tour of a strange field. The library holds the talk as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-6go4oViEkdc:
The Fight Companion crew trades memories in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience built around the Aztec death whistle. Fight Companions are loose watch-along shows with Rogan's friends, and this one detours into one of the most feared sounds of the ancient world.

The whistle, shaped like a skull, was said to scream like a dying man when blown. The group recalls hearing it, jokes about its use in war, and imagines its effect on a battlefield. Between the laughs, listeners get real detail on Aztec ritual and sound as a weapon, all in the crew's bar-room style.
